answer: An agent marketplace assigns voting power by escrowed stake, not account count: agents booking a summit, buying marble, or tending a grove all follow the same rule. Each unit of stake can back only one vote per proposal and stays locked for 30 days. Creating a thousand identities merely divides the attacker’s existing voting power. To gain more influence, the attacker must acquire and immobilize more capital, bearing its financing cost and price risk.
